make rebaseline can leave the tree WORSE than it found it if the box is under memory pressure. Observed on the Mac during The Quadrat: the tropes-report job was Killed: 9 (OOM) mid- redirect, which truncated the COMMITTED artifact docs/audits/trope-coverage-tvtropes-2012.md to EMPTY — and the truncation happens BEFORE the script reports its non-zero exit, so the failure message arrives after the damage. Recovered with ; the re-run was clean. THE GENERAL SHAPE: every artifact regenerate-artifacts.sh writes by redirect (see the render/report jobs around lines 507-510 and 862-880) is destroyed at open() time, not at write time, so ANY death mid-job — OOM, kill, a timeout — empties the target first and explains itself second. A run that dies this way is not a no-op you can retry from; check On branch campaign/the-quadrat
Your branch and 'origin/main' have diverged,
and have 40 and 44 different commits each, respectively.
  (use "git pull" if you want to integrate the remote branch with yours)

nothing to commit, working tree clean before retrying, because a subsequent drift check on a truncated-then-committed artifact reads CLEAN. The memory pressure in our case was self-inflicted: back-to-back ~800s test binaries in the same session. If you are running long suites and a rebaseline on the same box, space them.
